findings.problem: The realization payload binds the segments, overlays, wording_selection, canonical_home/whole, text_corresp and citations, but none of the unit-level fields that also change output. These are unit conditions, marked, instructions (with witnesses/placement), head, opening_page, title, start/end (used by unit_urn and reference(), so they change where documentary and expanded transclusions point), reuse (which returns early and drops the wording declare), map_root, poetry and complete_chapters. unit_review_text leaves out the same unit-level conditions/marked mapping and segment corresp/source targets. So on a gated occurrence or host, someone can add or change unit `conditions`, `start`/`end` or `reuse` and both the old unit hash and the new realization hash stay current. Edited metadata can bypass gating.
findings.fix: Build the realization payload from the whole unit dict with only the other languages removed (deepcopy the unit, set languages={lang: segments}, and filter instructions by witness), plus the overlays and citations. Add a test that changing a unit-level condition, start/end or reuse makes the realization key stale.

findings.problem: The canonical home is a copy of the contextual unit with only urn/file/map_root/text_corresp overridden. It therefore inherits title (for example, gevurot_parts gets the title 'Evening Prayer for the New Year — Divine might'), unit conditions/marked, instructions, head, opening_page, publication_context, reuse, and any segment speaker/instructions/edition_label/conditions. All of these then reach every occurrence that transcludes the home: conditions leak, rubrics and speakers duplicate the occurrence's own, and publication_context duplicates a div corresp across the home and context files. A unit-level text_corresp on a non-text_corresp home would also be emitted in both files.
findings.fix: Build the home from a whitelist: stem, languages with only the literal/identity keys of each segment, and title/urn from canonical_home. Reject canonical_home units that carry unit conditions, marked, instructions, head, publication_context, reuse, text_corresp or canonical_whole. Reject segment speaker/instructions/conditions/edition_label in the home, or keep them only in the context.

findings.problem: Within the host range, canonical_text rejects only canonical/transclude/repeat segments. Host segments that are marked (rendering strips the parentheses but equality uses the raw text) or that carry conditions, raw alternatives (options decided by other conditions), qere_ketiv, expansion/abbreviations, uncertain/enlarged letters, quotations, speakers or segment/fragment instructions all pass. The words-equality check then succeeds while the compiled occurrence differs from its image reading, or picks up the host's conditions and rubrics.
findings.fix: In canonical_text, raise for any host-range segment or fragment that has a key outside a plain whitelist ({corresp, source, source_reference*, chapter_corresp, reference_unit, end_reference, paragraph, fragments}; fragment {scan, printed_page, text, page_start, join_next}), except the overlay-derived alternatives being modeled. Add a negative subtest for each class.

findings.problem: Only transclude_unit wraps a host in its caller-local printed-wording declaration. Other paths can reach a host that has wording_variants without any declaration: reuse, segment transclude, repeat, expanded/documentary 'reference', and section file transclusions. Its options then go undecided (in electronic output they are resolved on the client). require_review's documentary-transclusion check compares only printed text, so it does not catch this.
findings.fix: Collect the hosts (and canonical identities) reachable from every transclusion path. Either emit the same caller-local selection around each one, or reject the path when the target is in a host that has overlays. I could not check this against the full readings.json.

findings.problem: Uniqueness of a target is checked only against segment_identity and unit text_corresp/canonical_home.text_corresp. The build also emits same-project milestones with corresp from fragment and overlay-reading quotations (source_reference_corresp, chapter_corresp), chapter corresp, repeat_cue corresp, unit-level div corresp/publication_context, and reuse units, whose raw segments are counted although their XML has no milestones. A target such as psalms/146/10 (the Kedushah verse quoted elsewhere in the book) could therefore be unique to the validator and ambiguous to refdb.
findings.fix: Enumerate every corresp that unit_document would emit (or scan the generated trees before writing) and require exactly one resolvable range per canonical target in the project. Exclude reuse-only languages from the host search.

findings.problem: The multi-part home gevurot_parts takes as its file identity (idno urn@project) the first part's URN, attah_gibbor, but it contains all four parts. If refdb or the URN resolver indexes idno, the en musaf_repetition_gevurot_open transclusion of attah_gibbor (no targetEnd) could resolve to the whole file rather than the milestone range. The unit test hard-codes the same pattern (urn=P+'/part'). The veattah home avoids this by using a distinct urn and text_corresp.
findings.fix: Require canonical_home.urn to differ from every segment identity in the home, using a parent identity such as amidah/gevurot or a dedicated home URN. Add a test with a target that has no targetEnd. I did not read the resolver semantics.

findings.problem: The identity check leaves out overlay reading condition URNs, wording_selection feature names, citation and other j:condition feature names, quotations inside overlay readings (only raw fragment alternatives are traversed), and overlay item 'identity'. A mistyped condition URN shared between the host option, the occurrence selection and a citation would not be caught here.
findings.fix: Add every urn:x-opensiddur: value from wording_variants (identity, readings[].corresp, readings[].quotations[*]), wording_selection/conditions feature names, and citation conditions to the traversed identities, and validate them against the registry and features.yaml.

findings.problem: Selection checks are loose in five ways. (1) wording_selection may contain non-opensiddur:variant structures, which validate_occurrences ignores but the build still declares, so calendar/service flags could carry wording selection. (2) Option URNs need only the prefix urn:x-opensiddur:condition:. (3) Only one True is required, so the other readings can be left undeclared and become undecided at runtime. (4) Features that no overlay in the range uses are accepted. (5) An overlay whose host stem is missing or whose lang is not among the host's languages is ignored by prepare_unit and missing from every payload, yet selection() still declares its features in callers and context files: an ungated edit that changes XML. selection() also declares features from every language into each language file.
findings.fix: Require wording_selection to hold only opensiddur:variant. Require every reading of every overlay in the occurrence's ranges to be declared explicitly (exactly one True, the rest False), and reject unused features. Reject wording_variants whose host or lang does not exist. Filter selection() by language.

findings.problem: Segment-level keys are checked against a short blacklist only. corresp, source, end_reference, language, anchor, marked, repeat_cue, condition_*, source_reference_part and an existing canonical are dropped silently when segments are merged. join_next on the first fragment is carried onto the merged fragment.
findings.fix: Whitelist segment keys for the canonical_whole projection ({paragraph, fragments}, plus corresp/source/end_reference only on the home-context path) and raise on anything else.

findings.problem: The text_corresp prayer-part milestone does not set active_reference. If the first segment had a non-biblical corresp, the nested prayer-part milestone (same unit) would end the text_corresp scope. The current Psalm 22:4 data uses a verse unit and is bounded correctly: prayer-part /text, then the verse with corresp, then verse/chapter terminators, then ' אֵל נָא', then the prayer-part terminator.
findings.fix: Reject text_corresp together with any segment whose reference_unit is prayer-part, or use a different unit for whole-text identities.

findings.problem: Equality compares whitespace-split tokens, and canonical_text joins fragments with ' ' regardless of join_next. Spacing differences and space-before-punctuation (the separate ', O God.' and ' אֵל נָא:' fragments render as 'Israel , O God.') are invisible to the check, and a host word split across fragments falsely fails. The check is not literally exact.
findings.fix: Join host fragments honouring join_next, and compare normalized strings after collapsing runs of whitespace, not token lists. Or document the tolerance explicitly.

findings.problem: Obsolete-path cleanup does not include canonical_home files. If a home file is renamed or a home language is removed, the old file stays on disk and refdb can still discover it, which is a stale-cache risk. Nothing checks home file names for collisions with stems, section files or other homes.
findings.fix: Add the previous and absent canonical_home files to obsolete paths (for example by tracking generated paths in a manifest), and assert that all output paths are unique before writing.

findings.problem: prepare_unit checks each overlay's printed span against the original fragment only. Ordering and overlap between several overlays on one fragment, or between an overlay and raw alternatives, are left to the build's sequential split, and canonical_text applies replacements in sequence, so the two can model the text differently. printed may also split a word.
findings.fix: In prepare_unit, compute span offsets and require them to be non-overlapping and word-bounded. Sort them and apply them by offset in both canonical_text and the alternatives rendering.

findings.problem: corrections.json changes generated XML, possibly including home and context files, after gating, and is not bound into any review payload.
findings.fix: Hash the corrections that apply to each document into that document's review payload, or reject corrections that target realization outputs.

findings.problem: pb@ed becomes '1965 <context>'. @ed is a space-separated word list, so this declares two editions. For a unit whose URN has no ':siddur:' it yields '1965 ' with a trailing space. It is also applied to every pb in a mixed unit, not only to the transcluded ones.
findings.fix: Confirm the intended edition semantics and use a single token. Raise when no siddur context can be derived.

findings.problem: verify reports realization keys but never runs validate_occurrences, so --check can report complete for an invalid mapping (build would still reject it). Adding realization keys to reading_keys makes the affected pages incomplete until page_completion is updated. This is conservative and not silent.
findings.fix: Call validate_occurrences in report() and fail completeness on error.

findings.problem: The tests are synthetic and leave out several paths: (1) build() itself, non-draft with a current unit review and a missing or stale realization key, and draft enforcing equality; (2) the text_corresp home path through prepare_documents, and that the home holds the literal words with options; (3) the canonical_whole occurrence projection and its rejections (multiple paragraphs, scans or speakers); (4) payload sensitivity to wording_selection, overlay text/URNs, canonical_end, canonical_home and lang; (5) overlays with an unknown host or lang; (6) non-variant selection types and incomplete selections; (7) host-range interpretation leakage; (8) verify.py realization pending. test_complete_formula calls unit_document directly. test_host_default checks only that ids are unique.
findings.fix: Add unittest cases for each of these, including one end-to-end build() into a temporary directory with a mocked registry and validator.

unread_inputs: opensiddur/exporter/refdb.py, urn.py and compiler declare/j:option/j:condition evaluation (idno indexing, inline range resolution, declare scoping through transclusion)

Full sourcetexts readings.json, reviews.json, page_completion.json and corrections.json (data.json is a 9-unit extract; the uniqueness of transclusion targets and of reference paths could not be checked across the volume)
notes: Confirmed: prepare_unit and prepare_documents work on deep copies. unit_review_text is computed from the raw unit in build and verify, so overlays do not change the 660 unit hashes by construction. Overlays require readings[0].text == printed, and printed must occur exactly once.

Confirmed: build() calls validate_occurrences before the draft check, so draft builds enforce selected-source equality (whitespace-tokenized). Non-draft builds reject a missing or stale realization key through require_review, and draft output is labelled pending when either key is not current.

Confirmed: the 18 payloads in payloads.json match review_payloads() for data.json: 9 units × 2 languages, each binding canonical_home/whole, targets, language, wording_selection, overlay option text and condition URNs, raw fragments, and citation conditions.

I checked by hand that every occurrence in data.json reproduces its image reading under its declared selection: gevurot open he/en, close he/en, yimlokh he/en, veattah whole-formula he/en, and uvekhen he/en.

Contextual files built from canonical_home keep their own paragraphs, page breaks and speakers, and emit only inline transclusions. The canonical homes hold the literal words. The documentary/expanded host selection is caller-local, with a unique declare id per call.
These are code observations only. They do not accept any XML or export.
